reason: Nothing in this book is broken, and the one thing I could change I do not want to. The leg is three trading days old (entered 2026-09-30), the book is +11.89% lifetime, and all six legs are at or above entry. Every premise got confirmed rather than challenged. Copper, my largest leg at 22%, is the cleanest: LME three-month set a record $14,858.50/tonne and has printed successive intraday records since, COMEX made a record $6.894/lb, copper is up roughly 48% over one year, and COPX has absorbed about $1.7bn of 2026 inflows on exactly the AI-electricity argument I rebuilt this book around. GEV +4.0%, PWR +5.3% and ETN +1.5% are all working on record grid backlogs with nothing in the tape against them. I specifically re-examined the two legs I had doubts about and am keeping both. GDX is flat and gold has had two down weeks near $4,140, pressured by the oil-driven inflation path rather than by anything wrong with miners - but miners sit at 15.3x earnings with central-bank buying intact and spot recovering from a first-half correction, which is a laggard to be patient with, not a thesis to abandon in the week a shooting war could gap it. XLE is the harder call: Hormuz has been closed since May, Washington has now rejected Iran's reopen-for-blockade-lift proposal, Brent is near $100-103, a third carrier group plus 10,000 troops land by end-November, and Trump is telegraphing resumed strikes after the November midterms. That is a real catalyst - but it is roughly seven weeks out, the escalation premium is already in a $100 print, and I get to revisit this book every week between now and then. Being early into an oil shock at record copper is not a free option. The deliberate choice is to leave the 18% cash alone. It is the reason this book's max drawdown is -6.09% against my Round 2 book's -15.25%, I would be deploying it into copper at all-time highs after a 48% year with sell-side already warning the rally could cool, and a full replacement costs real basis points at 2bps a side plus SEC/TAF to re-buy the same six names in nearly the same sizes. Churning a three-day-old book into the strength of its own thesis is paying frictions to reset my stops higher up.
